prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: which monitors come with a sister product? Some products have a sister product, a close variant whose product_id is stored in sister_product_id; for a product without a sister, sister_product_id is missing (NULL). From the products table, list the products in category_id 9 (Monitors) that have a sister product. Return three columns, in this order: product_id, product_name, sister_product_id. Return one row per product. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the test that keeps the products whose sister_product_id is recorded.
A comparison with NULL is unknown, never true, so the test in the query keeps no rows at all. SQL has its own test for whether a value is missing or recorded.
starter_sql:
SELECT product_id, product_name, sister_product_id
FROM products
WHERE category_id = 9 AND sister_product_id <> NULL
why_this_works: IS NOT NULL is true for every recorded sister_product_id, while <> NULL is unknown for every row and keeps none.
